_comment: Fix-agent 7g (store-loop performance, item 1): same gating mechanism as `packages/core/bench/thresholds.json` (see that file's `_comment` for the methodology), applied to `apps/editor`'s OWN bench output (`bench/results.json`, produced by `apps/editor`'s `vitest bench`) instead of `packages/core`'s (`bench/core-results.json`) — `check-bench.ts` is invoked a second time against this pair from the root `check-bench` script. This is the store-LOOP-level gate `tasks.md` 7.15/7f.6 flagged as missing: the `PixelKernels`-scoped gates above measure a single stateless kernel call; these measure `core.slice.ts`'s ACTUAL per-dispatch cost (`storeDispatch` in `store-loop.bench.ts` mirrors that slice's real post-7g `snapshot()`-only-on-`structureChanged` logic exactly, not a simplified stand-in).
_comment_phase7g: MEASURED on this machine (pnpm run bench, warm — core constructed outside the timed loop, `warmupIterations: 50`) AFTER the 7g fix (DispatchResult.structureChanged lets the store skip snapshot() entirely for the pixel-only stroke.points calls that dominate this gesture): a 64px/1-frame/1-layer stroke gesture (begin + 20x4pt points + end) is Wasm ~1.65x SLOWER than TS end-to-end; the same gesture on a 256px/8-frame/8-layer document is ~2.14x SLOWER. This IS an improvement over the pre-fix behavior (the prior, unwired measurement: ~1.95x slower with an UNCONDITIONAL snapshot() on every dispatch) but does NOT flip the sign — for a SMALL per-call workload like `stroke.points` (a handful of points per call), the fixed per-call FFI/wasm-bindgen marshalling cost (argument boxing, the `Vec<u32>` result allocation + its JS-side decode into a `DispatchResult` object) is itself larger than the pixel work being done, and TS has no such per-call tax. Recorded honestly, not hidden: see `baseline-bench.md`'s 'Phase 7g' section and `design.md`'s 'Current status & follow-ups' section for the full writeup and what a future session could try (e.g. a batched multi-point-call-per-RAF-frame API, which this phase did not attempt — out of scope for a boundary-shape fix). Thresholds below are set just above the measured ratios (same honest-gate, fail-closed philosophy as every other threshold in this repo), not an aspirational target.
_comment_ci_noise: Budgets raised 2026-10-12 after the gate flaked on unchanged code: GitHub-hosted runners measured the 64px case anywhere from 1.69x to 2.52x and the 256px case from 1.72x to 2.95x across runs (PR #7 failed at 2.48x, then passed at 1.96x on rerun with the same commit). The local-machine budgets (2.0x / 2.6x) sat inside that noise band. New budgets sit above the worst CI measurement seen so far, so the gate still catches a real regression (e.g. a return to unconditional snapshot() per dispatch) without failing on runner jitter.
